notes: Summary: Enterprise trading analytics firm evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency chat and high-throughput reranking. Primary focus: predictable unit economics on a reserved GPU commitment.

Workload profile: conversational trading assistant (chat) + real-time news reranking + nightly embeddings job. Average interactive session = 450 tokens in/out, 12 requests/sec per 1000 concurrent users at peak window. Nightly batch embedding job ~10B tokens spread over 8 hours.
Latency & throughput targets: 95th percentile < 120ms for short-turn chat (<=256 tokens), p99 tail target < 250ms; sustained throughput target 2.5k requests/sec with spikes to 5k for 30s windows.
Model preferences: prefer open weights with quantized variants (Llama2-70B-int8 / custom finetune). Will consider Redwood-hosted model variants if cost/latency profile is favorable.
Capacity ask: initial reserved commit equivalent to 12 A100-80GB GPUs (burst to 18) or 8 H100 depending on price; desire autoscale burst policy with guaranteed reserved throughput.
Primary cost modeling assumptions used in evaluation:
- Baseline tokens: 12M tokens/day interactive + 1.25B tokens/nightly embeddings (batched)
- Utilization scenarios: conservative 45% (worst), expected 68%, aggressive 85% steady-state after 3-month ramp
- GPU cost inputs: commit pricing quoted in proposal v2 (see Drive link) - monthly commit for 12x A100 = $95,000/mo; 25x = $185,000/mo; wholesale on-demand equivalence ~2.2x higher.
Unit economics conclusions from POC (draft):
- At 68% utilization, committed 12-GPU plan yields ~$0.32 per 1k tokens (inference only) including infra, orchestration, and reserved amortized cost
- With 25-GPU commit targeting 85% utilization and increased batching, per-1k-token drops to ~$0.19 (embedding-heavy workloads drive better token economics),
- Host API on-demand compares at ~$0.45 per 1k tokens for same model family under observed latency constraints (no KV cache),
- Break-even horizon for the 12-GPU commit vs hosted: ~6.5 months given current token volumes and projected growth (sensitivity table in pricing deck)

Risk notes: insufficient KV cache hit-rate would raise tokens processed by ~14% and push breakeven out ~2 months. Nightly embeddings are highly compressible (batching gains) so committed plans favor larger embed workloads.
SLA / contract items under discussion:
- 99.95% uptime target requested by Catalyst; Redwood offered 99.9% with financial credits. Catalyst pushing for stepped credits at <99.95 with carveouts for force majeure.
- Latency SLOs: include p95/p99 reporting per route + tracer hooks; Catalyst wants per-token cost cap if tail latency exceeds agreed SLO during trading windows.
Operational asks from Catalyst:
- Token-level cost breakdowns in console and per-route dashboards
- Ability to pin specific model versions and automatic fallback to quantized variant under high load
- KMS ledger + key rotation schedule for private deployment, audit logs shipped to Catalyst SIEM
POC outcomes so far:
- Continuous batching + prefix caching reduced observed per-token GPU time by ~21% in simulated traffic; tail latency improved 18% vs initial baseline
- Embedding throughput on 8-GPU testbed achieved 70% of anticipated production throughput due to IO constraints; SE recommended dedicated NVMe layer for embeddings pipeline
Next steps (short):
- Deliver final committed pricing options with explicit unit economics per 1k tokens across utilization bands (Maya, 2026-03-14),
- Legal to provide counter-sample SLA language by 2026-03-18 (Catalyst legal owns redlines),
- SE to run 48-hour stress run on H100 variant to validate burst latency and update cost model (Carlos assigned)
